whatItDoes: Compares two strings and reports whether they are identical, shows the first point of difference, and calculates a similarity score using a Jaccard-style token overlap. Options cover case sensitivity, whitespace trimming, and line-by-line diff output.
whyItExists: Manually comparing strings — especially long generated values, config keys, or hash outputs — is tedious and error-prone. A comparator that pinpoints the exact difference and gives a numeric similarity makes quick work of the task.
whoShouldUse: Developers diffing config values or generated outputs, QA engineers verifying API responses, writers comparing document versions, and anyone validating that two values match.
useCases: Verify two API responses or configuration values are equal
Find the first differing character in two long strings
Quantify how similar two generated outputs are with a score
Diff two blocks of text line by line
Spot-check that two environments return identical config values
instructions: Paste the first string into the left input
Paste the second string into the right input
Toggle case sensitivity and whitespace trimming as needed
Read the equality result, first-difference location, and similarity score
Switch to line-diff view to see added and removed lines
Re-run after normalizing whitespace if a false mismatch appears
examples: Line diff: line 2 removed, line 3 added
bestPractices: Normalize whitespace before comparing when formatting may differ
Use case-insensitive comparison for identifiers that are case-insensitive
Prefer line-diff for comparing documents and files
Understand that similarity is a heuristic, not a semantic guarantee
Normalize Unicode (NFC) before comparing strings that may differ in combining characters
commonMistakes: Comparing strings with different trailing whitespace and reporting a false mismatch
Expecting case-insensitive behavior when case sensitivity is enabled
Using similarity scores to decide functional equality
Ignoring Unicode normalization differences (é vs e + combining accent)
Assuming the first-difference index counts characters rather than UTF-16 code units
faq: Is the comparison case-sensitive by default? — Yes, you can toggle it off for case-insensitive comparisons.
What does the similarity score mean? — It reflects token overlap on a 0-100 scale; higher means more shared content.
Does it handle Unicode? — Yes, it compares strings as text and highlights the differing position.
Is anything uploaded? — No, all comparison happens locally in your browser.
